raw_tool_response: User responded: status_model=Separate processing and approval statuses, transitions=Use separate processing and approval state machines. The following transitions apply to the first demonstrable release.  A. DOCUMENT PROCESSING TRANSITIONS  1. Uploaded → Processing    - Trigger: Successful upload and initial file validation.    - Actor: System.    - Failure: If validation fails, reject the upload and initiate the applicable failed-upload cleanup policy.    - Retrieval: Not eligible.  2. Processing → Indexed    - Trigger: Successful text extraction, normalization, chunking, embedding generation, and search indexing.    - Actor: Background processing service.    - Failure: Record the processing error, mark the document Failed, and prevent approval or retrieval.    - Retrieval: Not eligible until separately approved.  3. Processing → Failed    - Trigger: Unsupported content, extraction failure, embedding failure, indexing failure, or unrecoverable processing error.    - Actor: System.    - Failure handling: Record a safe error status, retain appropriate diagnostic metadata, and do not expose sensitive information in error messages.    - Retrieval: Not eligible.  4. Failed → Processing    - Trigger: An authorized Tenant Admin or designated knowledge manager initiates reprocessing after correcting the underlying issue.    - Failure: If reprocessing fails again, return to Failed and record the new attempt.    - Retrieval: Not eligible.  B. KNOWLEDGE APPROVAL TRANSITIONS  1. Draft → Pending Review    - Trigger: An authorized submitter completes submission of an indexed document for review.    - Actor: Submitting user.    - Retrieval: Not eligible.  2. Pending Review → Approved / Current    - Trigger: Successful independent review and explicit approval.    - Actor: An authorized knowledge reviewer who is not the original submitter.    - Preconditions: Processing status must be Indexed, and the document must pass applicable validation and review checks.    - Retrieval: Eligible only after approval, provided it remains current and authorized for the requesting tenant and user.  3. Pending Review → Rejected    - Trigger: Reviewer identifies incorrect, incomplete, unsafe, or unsuitable content.    - Actor: Authorized knowledge reviewer.    - Failure: Record the rejection reason and retain the review audit history.    - Retrieval: Not eligible.  4. Rejected → Draft    - Trigger: Authorized submitter creates a corrected revision for resubmission.    - Actor: Authorized submitter.    - Rule: The corrected revision must undergo processing and independent review again. Rejected content must never become searchable automatically.  5. Approved / Current → Superseded    - Trigger: A replacement version has successfully completed processing and received independent approval.    - Actor: System, following authorized reviewer approval of the replacement.    - Rule: The previous version must remain available as current until the replacement is successfully approved. Once superseded, it must immediately become ineligible for retrieval.  6. Approved / Current → Expired    - Trigger: An authorized knowledge reviewer or applicable approved lifecycle policy determines that the document is no longer valid.    - Actor: Authorized reviewer or system under an explicitly approved policy.    - Retrieval: Immediately excluded from retrieval.  C. GENERAL TRANSITION AND GOVERNANCE RULES  - Processing status and approval status must remain independent. Indexed must never imply Approved. - Only documents with Processing Status = Indexed and Approval Status = Approved / Current are eligible for AI retrieval. - Every retrieval must enforce tenant isolation and user-level authorization. - Submitters must not approve their own submissions or revisions. - Every state transition must record the document/version ID, previous state, new state, actor, timestamp, reason, and relevant processing/review outcome. - Invalid or unauthorized transitions must be rejected and audited. - Reprocessing or updating an approved document must not silently replace the currently approved version. - System failures must fail safely. Unapproved, failed, rejected, superseded, or expired content must never be used by AI.  The exact 180-day overdue-review behavior and detailed stale/conflicting knowledge criteria are intentionally deferred to Q3. Document deletion, purge timing, and retention behavior are reserved for Q5 and must follow the separately approved deletion policy., authority_matrix=Use tenant-scoped Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with clear separation between requesting an action, authorizing it, and executing it.  1. TENANT ADMIN - May upload and submit knowledge documents belonging to their own tenant. - May request reprocessing or reindexing of their tenant's documents. - May request document expiry or deletion. - May monitor processing status and review status. - Must not approve or review their own submissions. - Must not access or modify another tenant's knowledge.  2. KNOWLEDGE REVIEWER - Must be explicitly assigned or authorized for the relevant tenant. - May review submitted documents and approve or reject them. - May independently approve a corrected or reprocessed version. - May mark knowledge as expired when justified by the applicable knowledge lifecycle policy. - Must not approve documents or revisions submitted by themselves. - May not access knowledge belonging to other tenants unless separately authorized.  3. SUPPORT AGENT - May search and retrieve only approved/current knowledge authorized for their tenant and role. - May report incorrect, outdated, or conflicting knowledge for human review. - Must not approve, reject, expire, delete, or directly modify knowledge documents.  4. SUPPORT MANAGER - May use approved knowledge for authorized support activities. - May report knowledge issues for review. - Does not automatically receive knowledge upload, approval, or deletion permissions merely because of the Support Manager role.  5. PLATFORM ADMIN - May manage platform-level configuration and operational health. - Must not have routine access to tenant knowledge content. - Cross-tenant content access is prohibited by default and requires a separately authorized, time-limited, reasoned, and audited exception.  6. SYSTEM / BACKGROUND PROCESSING SERVICE - Executes authorized document processing, extraction, chunking, embedding, indexing, and reindexing operations. - Executes approved lifecycle-related automated actions only under explicitly defined policies. - Executes document purge operations according to the separately approved deletion and retention policy. - Cannot independently approve knowledge content or bypass human review.  GENERAL GOVERNANCE RULES  - All permissions must be enforced at the API and data-access levels, not merely through UI visibility. - All actions must be restricted to the relevant tenant. - Requesting an action does not automatically authorize or execute it. - Document approval must always be performed by an authorized reviewer other than the original submitter. - Reprocessing or reindexing must never automatically change a document's approval status. - Expiry and deletion requests must follow their applicable authorization and lifecycle policies. - All requests, approvals, rejections, executions, and failures must be recorded in an auditable history. - Unauthorized actions and invalid state transitions must be rejected.  The detailed deletion approval, purge execution, and retention rules remain subject to the separate Q5 decision. The overdue-review and stale/conflicting knowledge rules remain subject to Q3.  These permissions apply only within the user's authorized tenant and do not grant cross-tenant access., reviewer_eligibility=Only an explicitly designated Knowledge Reviewer assigned to the relevant tenant may approve or reject submitted knowledge documents.  The following rules apply:  1. An authorized Knowledge Reviewer who is different from the original submitter may review and approve or reject the document.  2. A Tenant Admin or Support Manager may perform knowledge approval only if they have been explicitly assigned the Knowledge Reviewer permission for that tenant. Their administrative or managerial role alone does not grant approval authority.  3. The original submitter must never approve their own document or revision, even if they also hold another privileged role.  4. Platform Admins must not have routine knowledge approval authority or bypass tenant-level review controls.  IF NO ELIGIBLE REVIEWER IS AVAILABLE:  - The document must remain in Pending Review status. - It must not become approved, current, or searchable by AI. - The system must notify the Tenant Admin that reviewer assignment or availability is required. - The Tenant Admin may assign another eligible, non-submitter Knowledge Reviewer within the same tenant. - If no eligible reviewer is available, the document must remain pending until an authorized reviewer becomes available. - No automatic approval, self-approval, or Platform Admin override is permitted. - All review assignments, approval decisions, rejections, and pending-review events must be recorded in the audit history.  A documented backup reviewer arrangement may be configured for each tenant, provided the backup reviewer is explicitly authorized and is not the document submitter.  These rules preserve separation of duties, tenant isolation, accountability, and the integrity of the Knowledge Base., rereview_policy=180-DAY KNOWLEDGE RE-REVIEW POLICY  1. START OF THE 180-DAY PERIOD - The 180-day review period starts from the date and time when a document version is first explicitly approved as Approved / Current by an authorized Knowledge Reviewer. - Upload, processing, indexing, reprocessing, or reindexing must not start or reset the review period. - Each newly approved document version has its own independent review period.  2. OWNERSHIP OF RE-REVIEW - The Tenant Admin is responsible for ensuring that knowledge documents within their tenant are assigned for timely review. - An explicitly assigned Knowledge Reviewer is responsible for performing the actual content review and making the approval or rejection decision. - The original submitter must not approve their own document or revision. - The system must track review due dates and notify the Tenant Admin and designated Knowledge Reviewer before and when a review becomes due.  3. OVERDUE REVIEW BEHAVIOR - When the 180-day review deadline is reached without a completed review, the document must be marked as Review Overdue / Pending Re-review. - Overdue documents must immediately become ineligible for AI retrieval and citation. - The document must remain stored and available for authorized human review, but must not be used to generate AI answers. - The system must notify the responsible Tenant Admin and Knowledge Reviewer. - No automatic approval or automatic extension is permitted. - An overdue document must become searchable again only after an authorized non-submitter Knowledge Reviewer completes the review and explicitly approves it as Approved / Current.  4. RESET RULE - Upon successful re-review and explicit approval, the review timestamp and next 180-day due date must be reset. - Rejection, reindexing, metadata updates, or processing retries must not reset the review period. - If the reviewer rejects or expires the document, it must remain excluded from AI retrieval according to its resulting lifecycle status.  5. AUDITABILITY - Record the last approval/review timestamp, next review due date, reviewer identity, review outcome, and relevant decision notes. - All overdue notifications, review actions, and status transitions must be auditable.  This policy applies independently to each approved document version and is enforced within the relevant tenant.  The 180-day overdue-review policy is separate from document deletion, purge, and retention policies, which are addressed under Q5., rationale=RATIONALE FOR KNOWLEDGE BASE LIFECYCLE AND AUTHORITY DECISIONS  The selected approach establishes a controlled, auditable, and tenant-isolated Knowledge Base lifecycle while maintaining a clear separation between technical document processing and business approval.  1. SEPARATE PROCESSING AND APPROVAL STATUSES  Document processing and knowledge approval represent two different responsibilities. Successful extraction, embedding, and indexing must never automatically authorize AI usage. Only documents that are successfully indexed, explicitly approved by an authorized non-submitter reviewer, and currently valid may be used for AI retrieval.  2. CONTROLLED LIFECYCLE TRANSITIONS  Explicit state transitions prevent invalid status changes, accidental publication of unapproved knowledge, and unintended use of failed or superseded documents. Revisions must undergo processing and independent review before becoming current. Existing approved versions remain available until their replacements are successfully approved.  3. ROLE-BASED AUTHORIZATION AND SEPARATION OF DUTIES  Tenant-scoped RBAC ensures that users can perform only their authorized actions within their own tenant. Separating submission, review, approval, and system execution reduces the risk of unauthorized knowledge publication. The absence of an eligible reviewer must never result in automatic approval or a security-control bypass.  4. INDEPENDENT REVIEW AND 180-DAY RE-REVIEW  The 180-day review cycle provides a defined freshness-control mechanism. Its start and reset are tied to explicit human approval rather than upload, indexing, or technical reprocessing. Overdue knowledge is temporarily excluded from AI retrieval until an authorized reviewer completes and approves the review. This prioritizes answer reliability over continued use of potentially outdated information.  5. AUDITABILITY AND ACCOUNTABILITY  Document submissions, processing outcomes, review assignments, approvals, rejections, expiry decisions, and lifecycle transitions must be traceable through audit records. Tenant boundaries and authorization must be enforced at the API and data-access levels.  EXPLICITLY DEFERRED DECISIONS  The following matters are intentionally deferred and are not implicitly decided through this Q2 response:  - Q3: Detailed definitions and detection criteria for stale, conflicting, and insufficient knowledge; human-review flag ownership, routing, and handling; and the precise behavior of knowledge affected by these conditions beyond the agreed 180-day overdue policy. - Q5: Document/version deletion scope, deletion authorization, purge-clock start, purge-failure handling, and retention/deletion rules for superseded, expired, and rejected content. - Detailed notification schedules and operational escalation arrangements may be refined through subsequent governed requirement clarification where necessary.  These deferrals do not weaken the decisions already made under Q2. The separate processing and approval model, non-submitter approval requirement, tenant-scoped role permissions, and 180-day overdue-review behavior remain applicable.  The decisions establish the first-release Knowledge Base governance baseline without prematurely finalizing unrelated policies. Any future changes must follow the applicable governed Requirement Update and approval process.

A Tenant Admin or Support Manager may perform knowledge approval only if they have been explicitly assigned the Knowledge Reviewer permission for that tenant. Their administrative or managerial role alone does not grant approval authority.  3. The original submitter must never approve their own document or revision, even if they also hold another privileged role.  4. Platform Admins must not have routine knowledge approval authority or bypass tenant-level review controls.  IF NO ELIGIBLE REVIEWER IS AVAILABLE:  - The document must remain in Pending Review status. - It must not become approved, current, or searchable by AI. - The system must notify the Tenant Admin that reviewer assignment or availability is required. - The Tenant Admin may assign another eligible, non-submitter Knowledge Reviewer within the same tenant. - If no eligible reviewer is available, the document must remain pending until an authorized reviewer becomes available. - No automatic approval, self-approval, or Platform Admin override is permitted. - All review assignments, approval decisions, rejections, and pending-review events must be recorded in the audit history.  A documented backup reviewer arrangement may be configured for each tenant, provided the backup reviewer is explicitly authorized and is not the document submitter.  These rules preserve separation of duties, tenant isolation, accountability, and the integrity of the Knowledge Base.,

rereview_policy.exact_rendered_segment: 180-DAY KNOWLEDGE RE-REVIEW POLICY  1. START OF THE 180-DAY PERIOD - The 180-day review period starts from the date and time when a document version is first explicitly approved as Approved / Current by an authorized Knowledge Reviewer. - Upload, processing, indexing, reprocessing, or reindexing must not start or reset the review period. - Each newly approved document version has its own independent review period.  2. OWNERSHIP OF RE-REVIEW - The Tenant Admin is responsible for ensuring that knowledge documents within their tenant are assigned for timely review. - An explicitly assigned Knowledge Reviewer is responsible for performing the actual content review and making the approval or rejection decision. - The original submitter must not approve their own document or revision. - The system must track review due dates and notify the Tenant Admin and designated Knowledge Reviewer before and when a review becomes due.  3. OVERDUE REVIEW BEHAVIOR - When the 180-day review deadline is reached without a completed review, the document must be marked as Review Overdue / Pending Re-review. - Overdue documents must immediately become ineligible for AI retrieval and citation. - The document must remain stored and available for authorized human review, but must not be used to generate AI answers. - The system must notify the responsible Tenant Admin and Knowledge Reviewer. - No automatic approval or automatic extension is permitted. - An overdue document must become searchable again only after an authorized non-submitter Knowledge Reviewer completes the review and explicitly approves it as Approved / Current.  4. RESET RULE - Upon successful re-review and explicit approval, the review timestamp and next 180-day due date must be reset. - Rejection, reindexing, metadata updates, or processing retries must not reset the review period. - If the reviewer rejects or expires the document, it must remain excluded from AI retrieval according to its resulting lifecycle status.  5. AUDITABILITY - Record the last approval/review timestamp, next review due date, reviewer identity, review outcome, and relevant decision notes. - All overdue notifications, review actions, and status transitions must be auditable.  This policy applies independently to each approved document version and is enforced within the relevant tenant.  The 180-day overdue-review policy is separate from document deletion, purge, and retention policies, which are addressed under Q5.,

rationale.exact_rendered_segment: RATIONALE FOR KNOWLEDGE BASE LIFECYCLE AND AUTHORITY DECISIONS  The selected approach establishes a controlled, auditable, and tenant-isolated Knowledge Base lifecycle while maintaining a clear separation between technical document processing and business approval.  1. SEPARATE PROCESSING AND APPROVAL STATUSES  Document processing and knowledge approval represent two different responsibilities. Successful extraction, embedding, and indexing must never automatically authorize AI usage. Only documents that are successfully indexed, explicitly approved by an authorized non-submitter reviewer, and currently valid may be used for AI retrieval.  2. CONTROLLED LIFECYCLE TRANSITIONS  Explicit state transitions prevent invalid status changes, accidental publication of unapproved knowledge, and unintended use of failed or superseded documents. Revisions must undergo processing and independent review before becoming current. Existing approved versions remain available until their replacements are successfully approved.  3. ROLE-BASED AUTHORIZATION AND SEPARATION OF DUTIES  Tenant-scoped RBAC ensures that users can perform only their authorized actions within their own tenant. Separating submission, review, approval, and system execution reduces the risk of unauthorized knowledge publication. The absence of an eligible reviewer must never result in automatic approval or a security-control bypass.  4. INDEPENDENT REVIEW AND 180-DAY RE-REVIEW  The 180-day review cycle provides a defined freshness-control mechanism. Its start and reset are tied to explicit human approval rather than upload, indexing, or technical reprocessing. Overdue knowledge is temporarily excluded from AI retrieval until an authorized reviewer completes and approves the review. This prioritizes answer reliability over continued use of potentially outdated information.  5. AUDITABILITY AND ACCOUNTABILITY  Document submissions, processing outcomes, review assignments, approvals, rejections, expiry decisions, and lifecycle transitions must be traceable through audit records. Tenant boundaries and authorization must be enforced at the API and data-access levels.  EXPLICITLY DEFERRED DECISIONS  The following matters are intentionally deferred and are not implicitly decided through this Q2 response:  - Q3: Detailed definitions and detection criteria for stale, conflicting, and insufficient knowledge; human-review flag ownership, routing, and handling; and the precise behavior of knowledge affected by these conditions beyond the agreed 180-day overdue policy. - Q5: Document/version deletion scope, deletion authorization, purge-clock start, purge-failure handling, and retention/deletion rules for superseded, expired, and rejected content. - Detailed notification schedules and operational escalation arrangements may be refined through subsequent governed requirement clarification where necessary.  These deferrals do not weaken the decisions already made under Q2. The separate processing and approval model, non-submitter approval requirement, tenant-scoped role permissions, and 180-day overdue-review behavior remain applicable.  The decisions establish the first-release Knowledge Base governance baseline without prematurely finalizing unrelated policies. Any future changes must follow the applicable governed Requirement Update and approval process.
